nodes.name: Modified Sol-Gel Synthesis Ta-RuO2
nodes.procedure: A mixture of ruthenium chloride and tantalum chloride in ethanol solution was precipitated by alginate. The formed gel was subsequently dried and then calcined in air to produce ruthenium-based oxides (see materials and methods for details). Such synthesis could be readily scaled up to kilogram production.
nodes.source_text: We synthesized the nanoparticulate Ta-RuO2 materials through a modified sol-gel method (24, 42). A mixture of ruthenium chloride and tantalum chloride in ethanol solution was precipitated by alginate. The formed gel was subsequently dried and then calcined in air to produce ruthenium-based oxides.

nodes.description: OER activity of RuO₂ thin films with different orientations by cyclic voltammetry
nodes.source_text: The OER current densities of pristine RuO₂ surface correlated strongly with the charge density, q*cathodic, indicating that the population of Ru sites was a dominant factor for the overall OER activity of RuO₂ thin films (Fig. 1C).

nodes.description: OER activity of Ta-RuO₂ thin films by cyclic voltammetry
nodes.source_text: Ta-RuO₂ (110) exhibited a geometric current density of 0.61 mA cm⁻² at 1.6 V versus reference hydrogen electrode (RHE), which was five-times higher than that of RuO₂ (110). Tafel plots... 78.3 mV dec⁻¹ for Ta-RuO₂ (110).

nodes.description: OER evaluation on rotating-disc electrode in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: Figure 4C shows the results of OER evaluation on a rotating-disc electrode in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ electrolyte. From the OER polarization curves, Ta₀.₁Ru₀.₉O₂₋ₓ shows a low overpotential of 226 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²... The TOF of Ta₀.₁Ru₀.₉O₂₋ₓ reached 0.086 s⁻¹ at an overpotential of 280 mV, which is... 20 times higher than that of commercial RuO₂ (0.004 s⁻¹).

nodes.description: Industrial single-cell PEM-WE stability at 1 A/cm²
nodes.source_text: A single-cell water electrolyzer... enabled electrolyzing current as large as 625 A at voltage as low as 1.704 V (Fig. 4F), delivering a rated power of 1 kW... During operation at a current density of 1 A cm⁻² Ta₀.₁Ru₀.₉O₂₋ₓ exhibited a constant working voltage for at least 2800 hours at a decay rate ∼14 μV hour⁻¹.
MEAs with Ta₀.₁Ru₀.₉O₂₋ₓ anode catalyst required 109 and 330 mV less in voltage to reach 1 A cm⁻² than did commercial RuO₂ and IrO₂ catalysts, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuO2 thin films showed similar thickness and RMS roughness according to XRR (fig. S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The films used in our experiments showed similar thickness and root mean square (RMS) roughness according to x-ray reflection (XRR) (fig. S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: RuO2 thin films showed RMS roughness values detailed in table S1; Ta-doped films showed slight increase in RMS roughness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: atomic force microscopy (fig. S2 and table S1)... A slight increase in RMS roughness was observed on Ta-doped films through atomic force microscopy (fig. S12 and table S4)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cathodic pseudocapacitive charge q*cathodic of RuO2 thin films correlates linearly (R=0.91) with calculated CUS Ru numbers: 10 nm⁻² (001), 7 nm⁻² (100), 5 nm⁻² (110), 7 nm⁻² (111).
nodes.evidence_snippet: We calculated the CUS as 10 nm⁻² for (001), 7 nm⁻² for (100), 5 nm⁻² for (110), and 7 nm⁻² for (111). As shown in Fig. 1B, the measured cathodic charge densities showed a good linear correlation with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.91

nodes.characterization_summary: RuO2 thin films show characteristic peaks for different orientations; after CV cycling, new peaks at 21.2° and 23.6° indicate RuO4 phase formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We used x-ray diffraction (XRD) to examine the thin films after 10 cycles of CV to understand the changes in electrode performance (Fig. 1D). Two new XRD peaks at 21.2° and 23.6° appeared

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern showing peak intensities

nodes.characterization_summary: RuO2(110) film 47 nm thick, grew epitaxially on MgO with atomically flat surface; after OER, surface corrosion with polycrystalline/amorphous RuOx species observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) (fig. S5A) maps and high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission election microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (fig. S5B) of the cross-section of pristine RuO2(110) film presented a highly crystalline... 47 nm in thickness

nodes.characterization_summary: RuO2(110) surface roughness increased from 1.3 nm pristine to 5.5 nm after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Synchrotron XRR data-fitting results indicated that the roughness of RuO2(110) surface changes from 1.3 nm for the pristine film to 5.5 nm after OER (fig. S7, A and B, and table S3)

nodes.characterization_summary: Identified new phase protruding from surface as high-valent Ru oxide clusters with low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We used grazing incidence diffraction (GID) as a surface-sensitive probe to identify the new phase as a species protruding out of the surface plane, most likely as high-valent Ru oxide clusters

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER, higher edge position and greater white-line intensity indicate increased Ru valence; FT-EXAFS shows reduced Ru-O bond length corresponding to RuO4 (1.7 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the x-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra (fig. S10), the thin film after OER had a higher edge position and greater white-line intensity... Fourier transform of the extended x-ray absorption fine structure revealed a slightly reduced Ru-O bond length

nodes.characterization_summary: Ta 4f binding energy ~26.3 eV reveals +5 valence state of Ta on RuO2 films.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (fig. S14) of these Ta-doped films showed that the binding energy of Ta 4f is ~26.3 eV revealing a +5 valence state of Ta on RuO2 films

nodes.characterization_summary: Ta-M4 edge signal at 1780-1795 eV confirms Ta doping in surface lattice of TaRuO2(110); Ta remains after OER test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy loss spectra (EELS) of surface atomic layers (Fig. 2C and fig. S13)... showed a distinct signal at 1780 to ~1795 eV which corresponds to the Ta-M4 edge

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ/ex situ Raman shows RuO2(110) Eg(536 cm⁻¹), A1g(649 cm⁻¹), B2g(715 cm⁻¹) modes with red shifts and decreased intensity during OER; Ta-RuO2 shows minimal changes and no RuO4 peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ and ex situ electrochemical Raman spectroscopy analysis (fig. S22) offered more evidence about degradation of RuO2... We clearly observed the vibration modes of Eg(536 cm⁻¹), A1g(649 cm⁻¹) and B2g(715 cm⁻¹)

The Ru dissolution rates for respective crystal faces were 11.9 (001), 5.3 (100), 44.5 (110), and 5.7 (111) ng hour⁻¹ for RuO2, and 3.9 (001), 2.4 (100), 21.8 (110), and 2.4 (111) ng hour⁻¹ for Ta-RuO2

nodes.characterization_summary: Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x shows (001) plane projection with interplanar distances 3.30 Å (110) and 2.32 Å (200).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4A shows a high-resolution HRTEM image for a projection of the Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x(001) plane in which the interplanar distances were 3.30 Å for (110) and 2.32 Å for (200)

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping shows Ru, Ta, O homogeneously distributed in Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Element mapping enabled by EDS indicates that Ru, Ta, and O were homogeneously distributed in Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x (Fig. 4B)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ta-RuO2(110) Rct = 478 ohms vs RuO2(110) Rct = 3392 ohms at 1.6 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ta-doped RuO2 films exhibited much smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct) compared with pure RuO2 films, i.e., Rct = 478 ohms for Ta-RuO2 (110) and Rct = 3392 ohms for RuO2 (110)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x exhibits porous and rough surface morphology providing high surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the TEM image (fig. S33B), Ta0.1Ru0.9O2-x exhibited a porous and rough surface morphology, which provides a high surface area
